summary: Iteration 32 — System sessions (Davamiyyət -> Sistem fəaliyyəti) feature fully tested. 10/10 backend tests passed. Frontend e2e: sidebar restructure (HR/Finance expandable groups), heartbeat-on-mount, system-sessions tab with full table, and logout -> /api/auth/logout flow all confirmed working.

minor.issue: Backend uses update_one() with filter {user_id, logout_at: None} but no sort — if a user has multiple stale open sessions, heartbeat/logout updates an arbitrary one rather than the most recent. In practice OK (browser keeps single session), but stale sessions accumulate forever (user_sessions collection has no TTL/cleanup). Recommend: add sort by login_at desc on the update OR add a cleanup job/TTL index.

issues: Aktiv müddət column shows '—' for most open sessions because last_active_at == login_at until heartbeat lands. Cosmetic — once first heartbeat fires (60s post-login), it shows duration. Could pre-compute (now - login_at) for is_open rows on backend so users see something immediately.

action_items: (Optional) Add periodic cleanup or TTL on user_sessions collection (sessions persist forever per design; could grow unbounded).
(Optional) Sort update_one() filter for heartbeat/logout by login_at desc so the most recent open session is always the one updated.
(Optional) On is_open rows, compute active_seconds against now() instead of last_active_at so the UI shows live duration without waiting for heartbeat.
critical_code_review_comments: Route ordering: GET /attendance/system-sessions is defined AFTER DELETE /attendance/{id} — safe (different methods), no shadowing.
Login path catches session-insert exceptions gracefully (try/except around insert_one) — login won't fail if user_sessions write breaks.
RBAC: /api/attendance/system-sessions requires hr:read — verified Sales user receives 403.
Frontend Sidebar.handleLogout fires POST /api/auth/logout BEFORE clearing localStorage and navigating — verified via network capture.
DashboardLayout heartbeat: fires on mount and every 60s. In dev StrictMode it double-fires on mount (cosmetic, harmless).
server.py is 4428 lines — exceeds the >700-line guideline; consider modularising routes (auth, attendance, hr, finance, etc.) into separate routers.

rca of the issue: No bugs blocking. The flagged minor issues (heartbeat update_one without sort, unbounded user_sessions growth, '—' display for fresh open sessions) are all low-impact edge cases worth tracking but not blockers.
